content.comment_body: I have 10 [product_name] devices connected in one network. Online testing works perfectly with [product_name] [version_no] 8.2. Since I switched to [version_no] 8.3 because I purchased new [product_name] devices, I started experiencing multiple problems with online testing on the older devices. Online test with the new [product_name] units using [version_no] 8.3 runs smoothly. I’m currently working with two versions of [product_name] software to manage all devices, but this is not a practical solution. I tried [version_no] 8.4, but the issue persists. Has anyone found a solution?

Hello, Could you clarify what specific problems you are facing? We expect that [version_no] 8.4 should address most minor issues. Please provide more details about the problems you are having with [product_name] devices.

Since [version_no] 8.3, online testing with older [product_name] units has become nearly impossible. Sometimes the connection works, sometimes it doesn't. If you do manage to connect, the software asks for a password even though none has been set. Once connected, everything runs very slowly. With [version_no] 8.2, everything works flawlessly. Currently, I use [version_no] 8.2 for my 10 older [product_name] controllers, and [version_no] 8.3 for the newer ones (8 units and more to follow). This is very inconvenient because all controllers are on the same network.

analysis.insight_summary: The user is encountering major communication and connectivity problems when using [product_name] software, starting with [version_no] 8.3 and later, to interact with older [product_name] hardware. These problems include unstable connections, unexpected password prompts, and slow performance during online testing. In contrast, [version_no] 8.2 works reliably. Having to use two versions of the software for different generations of hardware significantly increases frustration and complicates workflows.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects the latest [product_name] software to provide stable and consistent online testing for all hardware models without the need to alternate between different software versions.
